latest.schema: [date, value] monthly, value = Baa-10y spread in %

vintages.schema: [as_of, date, value] long — each as_of is the series AS KNOWN on that date
vintages.purpose: bracket 2020 COVID + 2022 rate shock; publication cutoff is honored (as_of 2020-04-01 knows only through 2020-03-01), which is the material look-ahead axis for this series (see publication_lag).
vintages.archive_start: ALFRED vintage archive for BAA10YM begins 2014-05-16 (146 vintage dates). No true 2008 real-time vintage exists — see caveat_2008.

vintage_self_check.contract: fred_vintage.assert_vintage_trustworthy — HTTP 200 is not proof (the trap). Verdict this run:
vintage_self_check.reason: no_revision_confirmed: the point-in-time mechanism is VERIFIED working (revised control GDPC1 differs vintage-vs-latest), yet BAA10YM is byte-identical across vintages -> genuinely NOT revised. Evidence, not assumption.
vintage_self_check.implication_for_killer_test: §3 (vintage vs latest) is satisfied WITH EVIDENCE: since revised==vintage for BAA10YM, any edge is identical under both -> no revision-based look-ahead. This confirms (not assumes) 工部尚书's 'market-price series ~unrevised' hypothesis.

signal_series.publication_lag: REMAINING look-ahead axis (revision is proven negligible; lag is not). BAA10YM for month M is published ~M+1 (the vintage cutoffs show this). 营缮 MUST decide at T using only data with publication_date<=T and execute T+1 — do not use month-M spread within month M. This is 营缮's to freeze in the runner (工部尚书's instruction); the vintage file's as_of cutoffs support honoring it.
signal_series.caveat_2008: No ALFRED vintage before 2014-05-16, so 2008 cannot be tested with a TRUE contemporaneous vintage — only latest. Given the evidenced no-revision above, latest==vintage for 2008 too, but that extrapolation (not an independent 2008 vintage) must be stated in the report; do not silently treat 2008 as vintage-verified.
